stem: A network engineer is comparing AWS Site-to-Site VPN and AWS Direct Connect for a hybrid design and wants two statements that correctly describe how the two can work together or independently. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Direct Connect encrypts traffic by default without needing a VPN
A Site-to-Site VPN connection uses two IPsec tunnels for redundancy
A Site-to-Site VPN generally offers more consistent bandwidth and latency than Direct Connect
A Site-to-Site VPN can run over a Direct Connect public virtual interface to add encryption to the dedicated link
Direct Connect is billed per connection-hour, the same way a Site-to-Site VPN connection is

rationale: A Site-to-Site VPN connection is built from two IPsec tunnels to a customer gateway for redundancy, which is a correct standalone fact about the service. The two services are also not mutually exclusive: a Site-to-Site VPN can run over a Direct Connect public virtual interface, layering IPsec encryption on top of the dedicated link, which correctly describes how they work together. Direct Connect is a dedicated private network connection, but it does not encrypt traffic itself; that is exactly why a VPN is sometimes layered on top of it, so the claim that it encrypts by default is backwards. The comparison on bandwidth and latency is also reversed: Direct Connect, not Site-to-Site VPN, is the one that offers more consistent bandwidth and latency because it bypasses the public internet. Site-to-Site VPN is billed per connection-hour, but Direct Connect's pricing is based on port-hours and data transfer for a dedicated connection, not the VPN's per-connection-hour model, so treating the two as billed the same way is incorrect.
